To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NPC1 is a eukaryote RND permease that transports acriflavine, but not cholesterol, out of the endosomal/ lysosomal system.

the Niemann-Pick type C1 (NPC) protein has homology to the resistance-nodulatioin-division (RNT) permease superfamily of prokaryotes, that it functions as a molecular pump, that the pump is proton motive force dependent and that the substrate for the NPC1 protein is acriflavine.
NPC1 functions as a proton motive force-dependent efflux pump that removes accumulated acriflavines from the endosomal and lysosomal compartments.

the molecular and cellular basis of cholesterol transport in mammalian cells.

we have identified the molecular defect in NPC1 disease, a defect that is likely to have a major impact on the development of new therapies.
